subject: SummitCX POC: action grid, success metrics & SDK/API routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@summitcx.com>, David Park <david.park@summitcx.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SummitCX POC: action grid, success metrics & SDK/API routing

Hi Sara / David —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clear framing of the evaluation goals. I promised a concise recap and a proposed action grid for the POC. Below is a single-page summary and proposed owners to keep momentum. I attached two artifacts: a starter success-metrics workbook and a draft API route matrix.

High-level POC goal:
- Validate Redwood inference for customer-facing chat routing (low-latency, <= 150ms median per turn) and extraction accuracy for entity + routing decisions (>= 92% on our test set).

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: median per-token latency <= 150ms during 95th percentile traffic pattern.
- Cost: inference spend <= $0.025 per conversation (target; flexible).
- Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on provided sample corpus; end-to-end routing accuracy >= 90%.
- Reliability: zero hard failures during 8-hour soak, and transparent error classification on Console.

Evaluation plan & timelines:
- Week 1 (Jun 28–Jul 2): SDK integration + sample traffic ingestion. Redwood provides a sample streaming client and short SDK walkthrough. (Owner: Summit engineering / Redwood SE).
- Week 2 (Jul 5–Jul 9): Run synthetic and sampled production-like traffic; collect latency/cost baselines. (Owner: Summit data + Redwood infra).
- Week 3 (Jul 12–Jul 16): Quality evals, calibration, and tool-calling verification. (Owner: Summit ML + Redwood applied ML).
- Week 4 (Jul 19–Jul 23): Acceptance window & final report. (Owner: joint).

Integration touchpoints (technical):
- SDK: JavaScript SDK + example Node stream included (we recommend streaming to reduce tokenization cost and improve tail latency).
- API routes: two routes to implement for the POC — /v1/chat/stream (real-time user messages) and /v1/predict/rerank (batch rerank for classification). See attached api-route-matrix.csv for mapping to Summit endpoints.
- Tool calling: Redwood supports function-calling via structured JSON. We'll validate one tool flow (entity extraction -> routing decision -> action).

Immediate asks for Summit team (by Friday Jun 25):
1) Confirm sample corpus delivery (S3 link or Drive).
2) Assign a primary eng owner and a secondary (for off-hours).
3) Confirm any IP/data residency constraints we should validate up front.

Attachments:
- poc-success-metrics.xlsx (starter sheets: latency, cost, quality thresholds)
- api-route-matrix.csv (mapping of Summit endpoints to Redwood routes)

Next step: if you confirm, I'll schedule a 30-min SDK walkthrough with our SE (Soojin) on Monday.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@summitcx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: David Park <david.park@summitcx.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitCX POC: action grid, success metrics & SDK/API routing

Thanks Ben — this is great and very actionable. A few quick confirmations: 

- We'll deliver a 3k-record sample corpus to the S3 bucket by EOD Friday (link to follow).
- Primary eng owner: David Park (cc'd). Secondary: myself (Sara).
- No special residency constraints; data in US only.

Couple of clarifying Qs: 
1) Can the streaming SDK handle intermittent network blips and reconnects without dropping the conversation context? We need to make sure client-side reconnect won't lose the KV cache context.
2) For function/tool calling, can Redwood call back to our internal webhook securely (mutual TLS) or should we proxy through a Redwood-managed endpoint?

Monday SDK walkthrough works for us — any time after 10am PT is fine.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sara

Sara Liu
Director, Product 
SummitCX
sara.liu@summitcx.com | +1 212-555-0443

- Soojin: lead SDK walkthrough + create a reconnect demo and doc (owner). Target: Mon 10:30am PT walkthrough.
- Marissa: validate webhook support for mTLS and list deployment options (proxy vs direct). Also prepare a short security note for the CISO checklist.
- Ben: coordinate S3 transfer, acceptance criteria sheet, and verify cost budget constraints.

Soojin / Marissa — can you confirm owners + whether we need an infra ticket to stand up a Redwood proxy endpoint for webhook testing? I'm happy to loop in infra if needed.

Thanks —
Ben
